dataflow.outcome: disproportionate local work and possible indexing stall or termination
dataflow.sink: CPU, heap, filesystem I/O, and index/store operation availability in the local KCS process
dataflow.source: attacker-controlled readable PDF bytes in an indexed local scope
dataflow.summary: scope PDF bytes -> raw byte gate -> lexical `/Page` count -> padded PDF page vector -> `PreparedUnit` hints -> per-hint whole-file `std::fs::read()` and `extract_pdf_text_pages()`

impact.why: The result is substantial local CPU, memory, and I/O amplification against indexing, but it is recoverable by removing the crafted file and does not expose credentials or execute code.

likelihood.why: The trigger is deterministic once the crafted readable PDF is indexed; it does not require race timing or privileged state access.

limitations: `max_input_bytes` bounds raw `S` but not derived `P` or `P` repeated extractions.
Wholly nontext PDFs route to OCR, so the crafted document must retain a readable text layer.
The LCS matrix branch is supporting amplification; the first-index repeated-parse sink is independently sufficient.

reachability.entrypoint: operator-run `kcs index` over an accepted direct-child PDF
reachability.outcome: local indexing availability loss for the affected process/scope
preconditions: The PDF has enough readable text to avoid the wholly-scanned OCR fallback.
The operator indexes the affected scope.
reachability.summary: The path is part of ordinary offline indexing and needs no listener, remote service, credentials, privilege escalation, persistence, or timing race.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust content contributor supplies a crafted readable PDF in a scope the operator indexes. The ordinary index path admits the file under the raw byte cap, converts false `/Page` prefixes into logical pages, creates one unit per padded page, and then performs repeated full-document PDF extraction for each derived hint.

codeEvidence.explanation: The closest control is a raw byte-size cap. After an accepted file passes that cap, its bytes and pathname enter `prepare_units()` without a separate logical page, unit, or parse-work ceiling.
codeEvidence.label: Ordinary indexing enforces bytes, then prepares the accepted PDF

codeEvidence.explanation: `pdf_page_count_in_text()` counts textual `/Page` matches in lossy-decoded input. It suppresses `/Pages`, but it does not require a token boundary or structural page object, so `/PageX` is counted and no page ceiling is enforced.
codeEvidence.label: Loose `/Page` prefixes define the page count

codeEvidence.explanation: For a readable PDF, the pipeline trusts `page_count` and pads the extracted page vector with empty strings until its length equals the attacker-inflated lexical count.
codeEvidence.label: The pipeline pads extracted pages to the lexical count

codeEvidence.explanation: `unit_count` follows the padded vector length, so every false page marker can become a unit, hash, fingerprint, page number, and later markdown hint.
codeEvidence.label: One `PreparedUnit` is allocated and hashed per padded page

codeEvidence.code:
let hints = request
    .prepared_unit_hint
    .clone()
    .unwrap_or_else(|| vec![default_hint(&request.raw.raw_hash)]);
let source_text = read_source_text(&request);
// ...
Ok(MarkdownizeResponse {
    mode_used: MarkdownizeMode::Full,
    updated_units: hints
        .iter()
        .map(|hint| markdown_unit_from_hint(hint, &request, source_text.as_deref()))
        .collect(),
    unchanged_unit_keys: Vec::new(),
    added_units: Vec::new(),
    removed_unit_keys: Vec::new(),
    evidence_pointers: Vec::new(),
    fallback_to_full: false,
    reason: None,
})
codeEvidence.explanation: The inflated prepared-unit vector becomes an equally inflated hint iterator. `read_source_text()` has already extracted the PDF once before this loop.
codeEvidence.label: Full markdownization maps every prepared hint

codeEvidence.explanation: For each hint, the adapter opens `request.raw.path`, reads the full PDF, rebuilds the page vector, and selects one page. With `P` inflated hints, this is at least `P` whole-file PDF reads/extractions plus the initial extraction.
codeEvidence.label: Every PDF hint reopens and reparses the whole file

codeEvidence.explanation: The repeated-parse sink is sufficient on first indexing. When prior units exist, the same inflated count can also feed the LCS matrix, adding `(m+1)*(n+1)` cells.
codeEvidence.label: Incremental mapping can add quadratic state

recommendations: Replace lexical `/Page` substring counting with validated page-tree traversal or a conservative bounded fallback.
Enforce a configured maximum derived PDF page/unit count before padding vectors or materializing `PreparedUnit`s.
Carry a verified page vector or byte snapshot through markdownization so page hints never reopen and reparse the whole file independently.
Degrade suspicious PDFs to a single file-level unit, controlled skip/error, or safer OCR path instead of trusting non-structural page markers.
Retain independent `(m, n)` bounds for `map_units()` so incremental LCS cannot amplify large unit sets.
regression_tests: A PDF containing `/PageX` false markers must not derive one page per marker.
A readable PDF with many false markers must produce a bounded unit count or a controlled skip/error.
Markdownization of multiple PDF hints must perform one PDF read/extraction per request, not one per hint.
A valid PDF below the configured page limit must still produce stable page units.
Incremental mapping must reject or cap large old/new unit matrices independently of PDF parser fixes.
remediation.summary: Structurally validate and cap PDF page/unit count, parse each PDF once into a bounded page representation, and reuse that representation for all hints. Keep a separate LCS work/cell cap for incremental mapping.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that a PDF page count used for allocation and repeated parsing must be structural, bounded, and shared across consumers. KCS instead enforces only a raw byte cap, counts loose `/Page` prefixes, pads page vectors to that count, materializes one unit per padded entry, and then reparses the full PDF for every derived hint.

severity.rationale: Medium local availability impact combined with high deterministic likelihood maps to Medium/P2. The absence of code execution, credential access, network exposure, or durable cross-scope corruption keeps the finding below High.

summary: KCS accepts PDFs under a raw byte-size gate, but its deterministic PDF path derives page count from loose textual `/Page` prefixes. That count pads the page vector, creates one `PreparedUnit` per page, and then drives markdownization that reopens and reparses the whole PDF for each hint. A small readable PDF with many false `/PageX` markers can therefore turn admitted bytes into disproportionate CPU, heap, filesystem I/O, and index availability loss.
title: Deterministic PDF handling reparses the whole file once per page

assertions: The lexical counter counts `/PageX` and other non-structural `/Page` prefixes.
A PDF with one readable text literal remains on the deterministic path and is padded to the lexical count.
Prepared and markdown unit counts follow the inflated page count.
The adapter performs one initial PDF extraction plus one full read/extraction per derived hint.
limitations: No unsafe stress-size input was run.
The largest practical marker count and host-specific wall-clock/RSS impact were not measured.
The impact is local availability, not code execution, credential access, or external send.
validation.method: static source trace plus bounded target-runtime attack/control exercise
validation.summary: The saved target-runtime control used one readable PDF-like input with 63 false `/PageX` markers. It produced 64 prepared units, 64 markdown units, and a source-trace minimum of 65 whole-file PDF extractions from 490 bytes; the 49-byte honest control produced one unit and two extractions. No stress-size input, external endpoint, credential, or production store was used.
